source_text: Hoc ergo "generi humano inflictum vulnus a diabolo, quidquid per illud nascitur, cogit esse sub diabolo, tamquam de suo frutice fructum iure decerpat" [n159] . Haec verba de libro meo tibi refellenda posuisti: quibus ita insidiaris, tamquam "naturae humanae auctorem dixerim diabolum, et ipsius qua homo constat substantiae conditorem"
pass_a_gloss: This therefore 'wound inflicted on the human race by the devil compels whatever is born through it to be under the devil, as if from his own shrub he plucks the fruit by right'. These words from my book you placed for yourself to be refuted: which you so ambush, as if 'I had said the devil the author of human nature, and the founder of the very substance by which man consists'.
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “So ‘this wound, inflicted on the human race by the devil, compels whatever is born through it to be under the devil, as though he were rightfully picking fruit from his own shrub.’ You set out these words from my book to refute them, and you lie in wait for them as though I had said ‘that the devil is the author of human nature, and the maker of the very substance of which a human being consists.’”

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
